issues.t: Takata airbag inflators can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. In a crash, the driver or passenger airbag inflator can burst and throw metal fragments at the people inside.
issues.why: The Takata inflators in these trucks can build too much pressure when they deploy. Mazda recalled 2004-2006 B-Series trucks for both front airbags, and told owners of 2006 trucks not to drive them until repaired (campaigns 17V806, 17V807, 18V038, 18V039).
issues.next: Stop driving the truck and contact a Mazda dealer to check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. The fix is free and Mazda can arrange towing.

issues.t: Replacement airbag inflator installed backward (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms. In a crash, the passenger airbag might not inflate as designed.
issues.why: During earlier Takata recall repairs, some replacement passenger inflators were installed the wrong way around. Mazda recalled about 12,700 trucks to check and reinstall them (campaign 23V837).
issues.next: Even if your truck already had the Takata repair, check your VIN and book the free inspection.

issues.t: Takata airbag inflators degrade with age (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. In a crash, an aged airbag inflator could rupture and spray metal fragments.
issues.why: Takata inflator propellant breaks down after long exposure to heat and humidity. Mazda recalled the passenger inflator on 2007-2009 trucks and later the driver inflator too (campaigns 16V499, 17V013, 18V016, 21V162).
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls and have a Mazda dealer replace the inflators for free right away.

issues.t: Cruise control switch can overheat and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or smoke from the driver side of the engine bay, sometimes even with the truck parked and off.
issues.why: The cruise control deactivation switch on the brake master cylinder can leak brake fluid inside, then overheat and burn. Mazda recalled affected trucks to add a fused wiring harness (campaigns 07V347 and 09V414).
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for these recalls and have the fused harness installed. If you smell burning, park away from buildings and have it checked.

issues.t: Throttle may stick when cruise control is turned off (recall)
issues.sym: After you turn off or cancel cruise control, the engine does not return to idle and the truck keeps pulling.
issues.why: The cruise control cable could catch on the speed control servo pulley and hold the throttle open. Mazda recalled about 22,000 trucks built January 1998 to March 1999 to replace the cables (campaign 99V062).
issues.next: Do not use cruise control until the recall is done. If the throttle sticks, shift to neutral, brake firmly and pull over.

issues.t: Timing chain rattle on the 4.0L SOHC
issues.sym: A rattling or buzzing from the engine, loudest on cold starts and around 2,400-3,000 rpm. Later, a check engine light or rough running.
issues.why: The plastic timing chain guides and tensioners wear out and break. Early engines had poorly designed guides; later ones wear at high miles. A broken guide can drop debris into the oil pan and let a chain fail.
issues.next: Do not ignore the rattle. Have a shop confirm which chain is noisy. Ford released a redesigned front cassette; fixing the rear chain needs the engine pulled, so earlier is better.

issues.t: Worn ball joints and control arms
issues.sym: Clunking over bumps, wandering steering, uneven tire wear, or a front end that feels loose.
issues.why: Ball joints are the most reported repair on these trucks, wearing out along with the control arm bushings and tie rod ends.
issues.next: Have the front end checked for play. A badly worn ball joint can separate, so do not put it off.

issues.t: Front wheel bearing noise
issues.sym: A humming or grinding noise that rises with speed, sometimes with a wobble or play in the wheel.
issues.why: The front wheel bearings and hubs wear out, sometimes early when water gets into them.
issues.next: Have the wheel checked for play. A failed bearing can lock up or let the wheel wobble.

issues.t: Rusted brake lines leaking
issues.sym: Brake fluid wetness near a wheel or under the truck, a soft or sinking brake pedal, or the brake light on.
issues.why: Steel brake lines rust through, especially in road-salt states. Brake lines are one of the top repairs owners report.
issues.next: If the brake pedal sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. If the pedal goes soft, do not drive. Have all lines inspected, since others are usually close to failing too.

issues.t: Rusted frame and leaf spring hangers
issues.sym: Clunks from the rear, the bed sitting crooked, or visible rust and flaking around the rear spring shackles and frame.
issues.why: Owners report rotted rear leaf spring shackles, brackets and frame sections on these trucks, mostly in rust-belt states.
issues.next: Have the frame and spring mounts inspected from underneath. Badly rotted mounts can fail and need welding or replacement.

issues.t: In-tank fuel pump failure
issues.sym: The truck cranks but will not start, or it sputters and dies, especially when hot or low on fuel.
issues.why: The electric fuel pump inside the tank wears out. It is among the commonly reported repairs.
issues.next: Listen for the pump hum when you turn the key, and have fuel pressure tested before replacing it.

issues.t: Clutch slave cylinder leaking
issues.sym: On manual trucks, the clutch pedal goes soft, sinks, or the truck is hard to shift and grinds.
issues.why: The clutch slave cylinder leaks. On these trucks it sits inside the bell housing, so the transmission has to come out to replace it.
issues.next: Check the clutch fluid level. If it keeps dropping, replace the slave cylinder and usually the clutch at the same time, since the work overlaps.

issues.t: Cracked PCV hose causes check engine light
issues.sym: Check engine light with lean codes, rough idle, or a whistling sound.
issues.why: The crankcase ventilation (PCV) hose cracks with age and lets in air the engine computer does not expect.
issues.next: Have the PCV hose inspected during diagnosis. It is a small part.

issues.t: Plastic thermostat housing leaks coolant
issues.sym: Coolant drips or crusty residue near the thermostat at the front of the engine, and low coolant.
issues.why: The plastic thermostat housing can split at its seam with age and heat.
issues.next: Replace the housing and thermostat and top up the coolant before the engine overheats.

issues.t: Radiator leak and overheating
issues.sym: The temperature gauge rising, coolant under the front of the truck, or steam from the grille.
issues.why: The radiator develops leaks with age, and hoses and fittings crack.
issues.next: Stop if the engine overheats. Have the cooling system pressure tested and the leak fixed.

issues.t: Oil pressure gauge erratic or reading wrong
issues.sym: The oil pressure gauge drops to zero, flickers or reads high while the engine runs normally.
issues.why: The oil pressure sending unit fails, giving false readings.
issues.next: Have real oil pressure checked with a mechanical gauge first. If pressure is fine, replace the sender.

issues.t: Check engine light from EGR valve or DPFE sensor
issues.sym: Check engine light with an EGR code, rough idle, or pinging when accelerating.
issues.why: The exhaust gas recirculation valve, its tube, or the pressure sensor that monitors it (DPFE) fails or clogs.
issues.next: Have the code read and the DPFE sensor tested; it is often the part at fault.

issues.t: Rear differential pinion seal leak
issues.sym: Gear oil wetness on the front of the rear axle and drips under the truck.
issues.why: The pinion seal where the driveshaft meets the axle wears out.
issues.next: Check the axle oil level and replace the seal before the gears run low on oil.

issues.t: Driveshaft U-joint wear and clunk
issues.sym: A clunk when shifting into gear or taking off, or a vibration at speed.
issues.why: Driveshaft universal joints wear out and the slip joint can dry out.
issues.next: Have the U-joints checked for play and greased. A failed U-joint can let the driveshaft drop.

issues.t: Blower works only on high or not at all
issues.sym: The heater and A/C fan works only on the top setting, or not at all.
issues.why: The blower motor resistor fails, cutting out the lower fan speeds.
issues.next: Replace the resistor; if the fan does not run on any speed, have the motor and fuse checked.

issues.t: A/C blowing warm
issues.sym: The air conditioning blows warm or only cool, and the compressor clutch may not engage.
issues.why: A/C compressors, clutches, relays and hoses wear out and leak refrigerant with age.
issues.next: Have the system leak-tested and the compressor clutch and relay checked before replacing the compressor.

issues.t: Automatic transmission hard shifts or no reverse
issues.sym: Harsh or delayed shifts, trouble shifting, or reverse stops working.
issues.why: Owners report automatic transmissions on high-mileage trucks losing reverse and shifting hard as internal parts wear.
issues.next: Check fluid level and condition first. Have a transmission shop diagnose it before it fails completely.

issues.t: No-start from worn starter or weak battery
issues.sym: A click or slow crank when you turn the key, or nothing at all.
issues.why: Starters and batteries wear out on these trucks; owners report replacing both after no-starts.
issues.next: Have the battery and charging system tested first, then the starter.
